recreation_brief: 1. Create a new blank slide with a light gray/white background (#F2F2F2). 2. Draw a rectangle with no fill and a thin (1-1.5pt) dark-red (#C00000) outline spanning from about 5% to 95% of slide width and 7% to 95% of slide height, to serve as a decorative frame. 3. Insert a text box centered horizontally at roughly 40-58% of slide height; type 'Parallelization' on line 1 and 'Implementation Issues' on line 2, in bold sans-serif (e.g., Arial), dark red (#C00000), approx. 40pt, centered alignment. 4. In the top-right corner (approx. 88-93% width, 10-17% height), draw a small oval with yellow fill (#FFFF99) and a purple outline (#7030A0); add the text '7' centered inside in small dark gray (#333333) sans-serif. 5. Draw a solid black (#000000) rectangle strip across the full bottom edge of the slide, about 3-4% of slide height tall. 6. Leave the rest of the slide empty — there are no bullets, images, charts, or equations. 7. Optionally note: do not add a mouse cursor; that was a recording artifact.
